turns.zh: 它就像一个黑洞， sort of 在吸入所有资本，以及越来越多的所有资本开支（capex）和资源。而且，你知道，我觉得它最终会自我坍缩，因为并不存在任何一种利润模型，能够为那些前沿实验室保留任何可持续的利润率——在那里你至少有三家实验室，全都在竞争要在任何一个时点拥有最好的模型。

turns.en: The costs to train the models go up substantially every round. If anthropic falls behind, the cost for me to switch from anthropic to open AI models is exactly zero or to Gemini models for, or to, you know- You think that you gotta switch a lot of stuff on your back end, no?
turns.zh: 训练模型的成本每一轮都大幅上升。如果 Anthropic 落后了，我从 Anthropic 切换到 OpenAI 模型、或者切换到 Gemini 模型的成本恰好是零，或者切换到，你知道——你会觉得你得在后端切换很多东西吧，不是吗？

turns.en: You do now because I don't now because of the way I've set up my machine. But like, yeah, it's like some enterprises would probably have to have.
turns.zh: 你现在确实得，因为我现在不用了，因为我搭建我这台机器的方式。但是的，就像，有些企业大概确实得这么做。

turns.en: It's one instead of zero, yeah. I mean, look, it's possible that companies are so fucking stupid that they fall into the Microsoft trap again.
turns.zh: 是一而不是零，是啊。我是说，看，也有可能公司蠢到再次掉进微软（Microsoft）的陷阱。

turns.en: And just like become trapped in open AI's captive office suite or anthropic's captive office suite or something. Like, if you're that fucking stupid, you can't be helped, right?
turns.zh: 然后就 kind of 被困在 OpenAI 的专属办公套件里，或者 Anthropic 的专属办公套件里，或者别的什么。就像，如果你真蠢到那个地步，那就没救了，对吧？

turns.en: But if you've got a grain of sand of scents in your head, then you realize that the actual models themselves are completely interchangeable.
turns.zh: 但只要你脑子里还有一粒沙子那么点常识，你就会意识到，那些模型本身是完全可以互换的。

turns.en: Codex is interchangeable for Claude Code, is interchangeable for Hermes, the open source model. All of these are completely interchangeable.
turns.zh: Codex 可以跟 Claude Code 互换，可以跟 Hermes 这个开源模型互换。所有这些都可以完全互换。

turns.en: And there is, so there is absolutely no competitive moat for any of these frontier labs. The only spark of hope is, so this is just like a pure gamble.
turns.zh: 而且，所以这些前沿实验室中的任何一家都绝对没有任何竞争护城河（moat）。唯一的一线希望是，所以这就纯粹是一场赌博。

turns.en: You'll be able to own all three labs because one of them might achieve RSI and that RSI will allow that company, they'll get it sufficiently far in advance of the other companies, that they will then go to become Tyrell Corp from Blade Runner and like, you know, just like own everything, right?
turns.zh: 你将能够同时拥有这三家实验室，因为其中一家可能会实现 RSI，而那个 RSI 会让那家公司——它会足够领先于其他公司，领先得足够多，以至于它们随后就会变成《银翼杀手》（Blade Runner）里的 Tyrell 公司，就像，你知道，就此拥有一切，对吧？

turns.en: Which is a whole other type of dystopia. But like, I just don't buy it, it's such a terrible bet. And if that doesn't happen, then there's just no conceivable moat.
turns.zh: 那又是另一种反乌托邦（dystopia）了。但就像，我就是不买账，这是一场糟糕透顶的赌注。而如果那没有发生，那么就根本不存在任何说得通的护城河。

turns.en: And these companies are the fundraising mechanism, the dream that they're selling is a fundraising mechanism that keeps all of this recursive funding loop alive.
turns.zh: 而这些公司就是那台融资机器，它们兜售的那个梦想就是一台融资机器，让这整个递归的融资循环保持运转。

turns.en: Keeps the original AGI, the market, going hitting its target. So what personally, what does that look like? No stocks, stocks plus alts, right?
turns.zh: 让最初的那个 AGI——也就是市场——继续运转、达成它的目标。那么就个人而言，这会是什么样子？不持有股票，还是股票加上另类资产（alts），对吧？

turns.en: Like I'm investor, like, yes, this scares the hell out of me. I know this is a bubble, but what do I do? That was the same thing. I'm like, I think it's all gonna crash, but I invest it anyway.
turns.zh: 就像我作为一个投资者，就像，是的，这事儿把我吓得要死。我知道这是一个泡沫，但我该怎么办？那也是一样的。我就想，我觉得它全都会崩，但我还是照样投资了。

turns.en: Like, that's the trick of like, I can't just sit in my bunker and do nothing. I mean, I agree. And it's a bit weird for you and I, right? Because we own businesses that our businesses provide exposures to different strategies and different risks and different segments of the market that, you know, most investors just don't have that side of their balance sheet to factor into their personal investment portfolio, right?
turns.zh: 就像，这就是那个两难之处，我不能就待在我的地堡里什么都不干。我是说，我同意。而且这对你我来说有点奇怪，对吧？因为我们各自拥有企业，而我们的企业提供了对不同策略、不同风险、不同市场区间的敞口，你知道，大多数投资者的资产负债表上并没有那一块可以计入他们个人的投资组合，对吧？

turns.en: But I mean, due to the return stacked lineup, I got a shitload of equity beta. You know, I've got a shitload of gold and Bitcoin beta. I've got a shitload of duration beta.
turns.zh: 但我是说，由于 Return Stacked 那条产品线，我有一大堆的股票贝塔。你知道，我有一大堆的黄金和比特币贝塔。我有一大堆的久期（duration）贝塔。

turns.en: I've also got a huge allocation to trend following. If it were up to me, I would own nothing but trend following. I would maybe stack some other, you know, features or factors or systematic strategies on top of a trend following program, but I would contain that exposure.
turns.zh: 我还有一个巨大的趋势跟踪配置。如果由着我，我会只持有趋势跟踪。我也许会在一个趋势跟踪程序之上再叠加一些其他的，你知道，特征或因子或系统化策略，但我会把那个敞口控制住。

turns.en: And I'm not wanna collateralize the futures portfolio with a mix of kind of gold and tips and nominal bonds, that sort of thing. But I mean, I personally think that the expected return on stocks here over the next decade or so is negative, maybe deeply negative.
turns.zh: 而且我不想用一篮子 kind of 黄金、TIPS（通胀保值债券）和名义债券之类的东西来给这个期货组合做抵押。但我是说，我个人认为，股票在这里未来十年左右的预期回报是负的，也许是深度负的。

turns.en: So I don't personally wanna own any stocks. And I have so much equity beta in my portfolio via the companies that I am an owner in that like I'm full up, right?
turns.zh: 所以我个人不想持有任何股票。而且通过我作为所有者之一的那些公司，我的投资组合里已经有了太多的股票贝塔，所以我已经满仓了，对吧？

turns.en: But I agree with you, if you're an investor and you need to make a decision, it's hard. There is, I think, a deep outside potential that the S&P does go on to eat the universe, you know?
turns.zh: 但我同意你说的，如果你是一个投资者、你需要做一个决定，那很难。我认为存在一种深深的、外在的可能性，就是标普 500 确实会继续'吃掉整个宇宙'，你知道？

turns.en: So like, you gotta have some exposure, I guess, to that outcome. I don't know what people who, you know, the 50% of Americans and 98% of humans who don't own any S&P are supposed to do in that situation.
turns.zh: 所以就像，你大概得对那个结果持有一些敞口。我不知道那些——你知道，那 50% 的美国人、98% 的人类——那些根本不持有任何标普 500 的人，在那种情况下该怎么办。

turns.en: Repeat those numbers. What is it, 58 of Americans, right? 95% of Americans don't own. It's actually, I think, 80% of Americans, I think the top 20% of Americans on all stocks and mutual funds, there's some that own like pension assets or something, but they don't really collect in the upside.
turns.zh: 把那些数字再说一遍。是多少来着，58% 的美国人，对吧？95% 的美国人没有持有。其实是，我想是 80% 的美国人，我想排名前 20% 的美国人持有所有的股票和共同基金，还有一些人持有 kind of 养老金资产之类的，但他们其实并没有真正享受到上涨的收益。

turns.en: In the upside on equity markets and pension portfolios accrues to the companies that sponsor the pensions, right? So because it's irrelevant to them.
turns.zh: 股市和养老金组合上涨的那部分收益，累积到了那些发起养老金计划的公司那里，对吧？所以说，因为它跟他们无关。

turns.en: Right, and they're just getting their AM. Yeah, so I personally think everyone should have the core allocation of their portfolio, should be diversified trend following portfolio, collateralized with cash-like assets, a diversified set of cash-like assets that can be resilient to different types of inflation and currency devaluation.
turns.zh: 对，而且他们只是拿到他们的那份管理费。是啊，所以我个人认为，每个人投资组合的核心配置都应该是一个分散化的趋势跟踪组合，用类现金资产做抵押，一组分散化的、能够抵御不同类型通胀和货币贬值的类现金资产。

turns.en: But I know that the vast majority of people just can't hold that behaviorally, so. Not just three X lever Nvidia and the new single stock future ETFs that are sure to come out, right?
turns.zh: 但我知道绝大多数人在行为上根本拿不住那个，所以。而不只是那种三倍杠杆 Nvidia，以及那些迟早会出来的新的单只股票期货 ETF，对吧？

turns.en: That's what's crazy, like there's literally a whole other side that's like, are you crazy? This is the bet of all bets, just full, push all your chips in on the AI trade, yeah.
turns.zh: 这才是疯狂的地方，就像真的还有完全相反的一拨人在说，你疯了吗？这是所有赌注里最大的那个赌注，就全押，把你所有的筹码都推到 AI 交易上，是啊。

turns.en: Sorry, I'm just, I'm a little wired for that. Right, yeah, but then it's a weird part. What do you guys say, get ready to stay poor or get used, what is it?
turns.zh: 抱歉，我只是有点太亢奋了。对，是啊，但然后就有一个奇怪的地方。你们那句怎么说来着，'准备好继续穷下去'，还是'习惯它'，是什么来着？

turns.en: I don't know, something. Yeah, yeah, but for you, and that's the other argument, when I tell friends this, I'm like, I think they're like, what are you talking about?
turns.zh: 我不知道，反正什么的。是啊是啊，但对你来说，而这正是另一个论点，当我把这个讲给朋友们听时，我就想，我觉得他们会想，你在说什么啊？

turns.en: This is like, improves my productivity so much more. I can go out and now I can send out 10 proposals and get back, like they're seeing it, they're seeing their business grow because of it.
turns.zh: 这东西把我的生产力提升了那么多。我可以出去，现在我能发出 10 份提案然后再收回来，就像他们看到了，他们看到自己的业务因为它在增长。

turns.en: And so I'm like, that's a little, I'm like, yes, but who did you replace, right, in that work? Like you haul it out to someone else and I'm like, not to make you feel bad, but like you didn't hire those people or you didn't get that architect to do that, whatever you did, you didn't pay that money to do that.
turns.zh: 所以我就想，那有点，我就想，是的，但你在那份工作里替代了谁，对吧？就像你把它甩给了别人，我就想，不是要让你难受，但就像你没有雇那些人，或者你没有请那个建筑师去做那件事，不管你做的是什么，你没有把那笔钱付给别人去做那件事。

turns.en: And that's the problem that you're not seeing. So it's gonna accrue to these business owners and stuff, but other businesses are gonna fail.
turns.zh: 而这正是你没有看到的问题。所以它会累积到这些企业主之类的人手里，但其他的企业会倒闭。

turns.en: Yeah, but this is a, I keep saying this, I was at a dinner with Demetri Kofinas, I don't know if you know him from Hidden Forces, but he hosts these fantastic genius dinners every so often.
turns.zh: 是啊，但这是一个，我一直这么说，我当时参加了一个晚宴，是 Demetri Kofinas 办的，我不知道你认不认识他，他来自 Hidden Forces，但他每隔一阵子就会办这些很棒的'天才晚宴'。

turns.en: And I was a guest there. And a lot of people had sort of similar views, similar concerns that AI is gonna eat a significant proportion of the labor market.
turns.zh: 我是那里的一个客人。很多人的观点 kind of 相似，担忧也相似，就是 AI 会吃掉相当大一部分的劳动力市场。

turns.en: Some people were invoking like creative destruction and this can be like a whole new class of jobs or whatever. And I kind of sit somewhere in the middle there, but also my big thrust is that this is a complete, this is not an inevitability, it's a failure of imagination.
turns.zh: 有些人搬出了'创造性破坏'（creative destruction），说这可能是全新一类的工作之类的。而我 kind of 处在中间某个位置，但我主要的论点是，这完全是——这不是一种必然性，而是一种想象力的失败。

turns.en: And the accrual of a systematic dismantling of state capacity and a unified vision for what America and the West wants to be. Like you can ask ChatGBT, what are the 10 or 15 documented, documented, extremely tightly specified major goals that the Chinese, the CCP have laid down to happen by 2030, to happen by 2035, stuff like have a permanent moon base on, have a permanent moon base, be able to- Plant a billion trees, they had all that stuff.
turns.zh: 而且是国家能力被系统性拆解、以及'美国和西方想要成为什么'这一统一愿景缺失的累积结果。就像你可以问 ChatGPT，中国、中共（CCP）已经确立的、要在 2030 年、2035 年之前实现的、有文件记载的、极其明确界定的那 10 到 15 个重大目标是什么，比如要有一个永久性的月球基地，要能够——种十亿棵树，他们把所有这些东西都列出来了。

turns.en: Yeah, plant a billion trees. To launch our own domestic fully-sourced commercial airliner, to have gotten resources from Mars and brought them back to Earth, to have created 50 gigawatts of power using nuclear fusion.
turns.zh: 是啊，种十亿棵树。要发射我们自己的、完全国内采购的商业客机，要从火星获取资源并把它们带回地球，要用核聚变创造出 50 吉瓦（gigawatts）的电力。

turns.en: Like they've got all these extremely specific missions that they have declared for their economy and then not just missions, but like submissions.
turns.zh: 就像他们为他们的经济体宣布了所有这一整套极其具体的使命，而且不只是使命，还有'子使命'（sub-missions）。

turns.en: In order to achieve this mission, we need these technology, you need a major leap in rocket propulsion. What are the major potential current branches of research that might lead to major leaps in rocket propulsion?
turns.zh: 为了实现这个使命，我们需要这些技术，你需要在火箭推进上有一次重大飞跃。当前有哪些主要的、潜在的研究分支可能会带来火箭推进上的重大飞跃？

turns.en: We're going, these are also priorities, right? Like this is a well-conceived, diverse set of bets, many of which will not work out or at least not work out the way that they expect.
turns.zh: 我们就去做，这些也都是优先级，对吧？就像这是一套构思良好、多样化的赌注，其中很多都不会成功，或者至少不会以他们预期的方式成功。

turns.en: But the pursuit of those missions will spin off an unbelievable supply of new scientific discoveries, new commercial and security applications, new ways to enhance citizen welfare, what have you.
turns.zh: 但对那些使命的追求，将会衍生出数量惊人的新科学发现、新的商业和安全应用、新的提升公民福祉的方式，诸如此类。

turns.en: This is a competent state with goals and a mission and the ability to coordinate resources through space and time, actually building a country, contrast to the type of nonsense that we're faced with.
turns.zh: 这是一个有目标、有使命、并且有能力跨越空间和时间来协调资源的称职的国家，是在真正地建设一个国家，与我们所面对的那种荒唐事形成对比。

turns.en: And it's not cause we can't, there's no magic. It's just we have- And you could argue they've learned that for months. We have an imagination for what we want.
turns.zh: 而且这不是因为我们做不到，这里面没有任何魔法。只是我们拥有——而且你可以论证说他们已经为此学习了几个月。我们对自己想要什么有一种想象力。

turns.en: It's like we're gonna go to the moon, right? Right. We have no idea how to do it, we're gonna do it. We have no idea how to coordinate anymore and we've done everything we can to destroy trust and capability in our institutions and our governing bodies.
turns.zh: 就像'我们要去月球'，对吧？对。我们不知道该怎么做到，但我们要去做。我们如今已经不知道该怎么协调了，而且我们已经竭尽所能地去摧毁对我们各个机构和治理主体的信任与能力。

turns.en: And so it's a mess. That's another weird part of like, we're so focused on building these data centers and getting to max like accelerating this curve where it seems like we're ignoring everything else.
turns.zh: 所以就是一团糟。这就是另一个奇怪的地方，就像，我们如此专注于建这些数据中心、专注于把这条曲线加速到极致，以至于我们似乎忽略了其他所有事情。

turns.en: Almost like a pancy of like, oh, once we get this figured out, it'll solve all those other problems. It's the paperclip maximizer. Yeah, it'll solve healthcare.
turns.zh: 几乎就像一种万灵药（panacea），就像，哦，等我们把这个搞定了，它会解决所有那些其他问题。这就是那个'回形针最大化器'。是啊，它会解决医疗保健。

turns.en: Like once we get, once this gets to, you know, ASI, like healthcare is a snap. We got cancer beat, we got this. Like, okay. So just build another data center, that's gonna save us.
turns.zh: 就像一旦我们达到，一旦这东西达到，你知道，ASI，那医疗保健就是小菜一碟。我们把癌症攻克了，这些我们都能搞定。就像，好吧。所以就再建一个数据中心，那会拯救我们。

turns.en: Exactly. I mean, look, there's a whole economic playbook, right? Mariana Mazzicato has been a real leader in this in how to structure state missions in a way that minimizes grift, maximizes innovation or productivity, results in the right balance of rewards to private actors in the corporate sector with spinoffs to society in the state.
turns.zh: 没错。我是说，看，有一整套经济学操作手册，对吧？Mariana Mazzucato 在这方面一直是一位真正的引领者，讲的是如何以这样一种方式来设计国家使命：最小化寻租贪腐（grift）、最大化创新或生产力，并在企业部门的私人行为者所获回报与社会及国家所得外溢之间达成恰当的平衡。

turns.en: Like this, it's not like any of this is a mystery. It all exists. We just exist in this fucked up ideology where only the market is allowed to decide what we want in our lives.
turns.zh: 就像这个，这并不是说这里面有任何谜团。这些东西全都存在。我们只是活在这样一种糟糕透顶的意识形态里：只允许市场来决定我们生活中想要什么。

turns.en: And any attempt to like set higher purpose goals or transcend what the market, I'm not saying that we should have central planning. Yeah, yeah.
turns.zh: 而任何想要设定更高目标、或者超越市场范畴的尝试——我并不是说我们应该搞中央计划。是啊是啊。

turns.en: We should have missions and incentivize the market to figure it out. I was, that's like my mom always asked me, what the market, which one mom?
turns.zh: 我们应该有各种使命，并激励市场去把它搞定。我，这就像我妈总问我，'什么市场，哪一个啊妈？'

turns.zh: 我们盯着 80 多。但对，这就是问题所在，我们没有，他们并没有让玉米市场上涨的激励。对。就像反过来也一样。我今天该为谁加油？

turns.zh: 我知道我从我爸那儿也得到同样的问题。愿上帝保佑他。我就说，我不知道。是啊，我不知道。反正昨天涨的那个，我们通常就想让它今天接着涨。

turns.en: That's right. Whatever went up over the last year, I kind of want to keep going. Exactly. All right, Adam, it's been fun and insightful. We'll put all the links in the show notes and talk to you next time.
turns.zh: 没错。过去一年涨的那个，我 kind of 就想让它接着涨。没错。好了，Adam，这次聊得又开心又有启发。我们会把所有链接放在节目备注里，下次再聊。

turns.zh: 太棒了。非常感谢你，Jeff。好了，本期节目就到这里。谢谢 Adam 来做客。谢谢 Jeff Berger 担任制作。我想我们下周会回来，但我不太确定。
